title: Torsion objects and orders invertible in a field
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and let $F\in\operatorname{Ab}(T_{\Et})$ be an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For a positive integer $n$, let
$$
F[n]=\ker(n\,\mathrm{id}_F:F\longrightarrow F)
$$
be the kernel sheaf [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], where $n\,\mathrm{id}_F$ acts by adding a section to itself $n$ times. Thus $F[n](U)=\{s\in F(U):ns=0\}$. The sheaf $F$ is called torsion in the local sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]: for every etale $U\to T$ and every $s\in F(U)$, there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and positive integers $n_i$ such that $n_i(s|_{U_i})=0$.

Let $K$ be a field and suppose that $T$ is a $K$-scheme. Define
$$
I_K=\{n\in\mathbf Z_{\ge1}:n\cdot1_K\ne0\},
$$
ordered by divisibility. An integer $n\in I_K$ is called invertible in $K$ (equivalently, $n\cdot1_K$ is a unit in $K$). A torsion sheaf $F$ has orders invertible in $K$ if for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and every $x\in F_{\bar t}$, with geometric stalk as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], some $n\in I_K$ satisfies $nx=0$. No common annihilator is required. The local torsion condition implies that every geometric stalk is a torsion abelian group [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]. In characteristic $p>0$, this says that the torsion stalks have no nonzero element killed by a power of $p$; in characteristic zero it imposes no condition beyond torsion.

Write $D(T_{\Et})=D(\operatorname{Ab}(T_{\Et}))$ and $\mathcal H^q(C)$ for its cohomology sheaves, as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. An object $C\in D(T_{\Et})$ has torsion cohomology with orders invertible in $K$ if, for every integer $q$, the abelian sheaf $\mathcal H^q(C)$ is torsion and has orders invertible in $K$ in the preceding sense.
